headline: Publishing and advising on what actually has to change before an enterprise can run agents.
context: Independent advisory and applied research on AI-native data architecture — MDM, data engineering and operating models rebuilt for a world where agents, not dashboards, are the primary consumers of enterprise data. Published as long-form strategy notes.

outcomes.text: Published strategy notes covering AI strategy vs. AI theatre, the AI investment ladder, AI-native MDM, data engineering rebuilt by AI, and the hybrid FSO-FSP operating model for CROs.

Developed the AI-native MDM thesis — replacing rules-based batch hubs with semantic matching, learned survivorship and event-driven settlement, with an 18-month strangler-fig migration path and a year-2 financial crossover model.

Mapped the agentic-era data engineering platform: an agent control plane and a context/semantic plane sitting over lineage, observability, evals, policy and unit cost — with the trust plane sequenced first, not last.
Advising leaders on where AI genuinely pays back, and where the honest answer is that the data foundation has to come first.

leadership: Framing complex architecture decisions for executive audiences — vendor reality checks, TCO models and migration sequencing written to be argued with, not admired.

headline: Enterprise AI platform and governance backbone for a top-3 global CRO running trials in 100+ countries.
context: Parexel is a $2B+ clinical research organisation. I owned enterprise data strategy, AI architecture and governance across clinical and commercial operations — scoping, pricing, scheduling, project management, finance, forecasting, clinical data management, site and investigator selection, and FSO/FSP resource management.

outcomes.text: Cut analyst research time by architecting and launching an enterprise AI platform using LLM and knowledge-graph technology for intelligent search, protocol summarisation and site/investigator insight across the global study portfolio — accelerating study start-up decisions.

Designed a Knowledge LLM pipeline joining structured clinical metadata to unstructured protocol documents through a RAG architecture, letting operational teams query trial intelligence in natural language with governed, auditable data access.
Reduced downstream reconciliation effort by architecting the data governance, MDM and data quality roadmap for global clinical operations, enabling audit-ready lineage across multi-study portfolios.
Established an Architecture Review Board governing every data platform investment across eight-plus business domains — preventing costly rework and holding regulatory alignment.
Accountable for delivery quality, budget oversight and risk mitigation across the enterprise data and AI architecture portfolio.

leadership: Provided executive-level coaching to senior architects and technical leads on solution quality, stakeholder engagement and enterprise alignment; owned architecture capability maturity and long-term talent strategy across the enterprise data domains.

headline: Technical leadership for a data products startup, and governance blueprints for its clients.
context: Provided solution architecture guidance and consulting services to a data products company and its enterprise clients across AWS and Azure.

outcomes.text: Designed data lakehouse and operational data store architectures on AWS and Azure, consolidating siloed sources into unified analytics-ready platforms and reducing client time-to-insight from weeks to days.
Delivered data governance blueprints — classification frameworks, metadata management and data catalog configurations — giving clients a structured path to regulatory-ready, trustworthy data assets.
Advised on data integration pipelines, MDM, data classification and cataloguing as part of end-to-end governance implementation.

leadership: Acted as the senior technical voice for a small company selling into large enterprises — translating client needs into practical architecture guidance and credible delivery estimates.

role: Advisory Director, Data & Analytics — Digital Lighthouse
headline: Five years running data management programmes for Fortune 500 clients — architecture, delivery, P&L and the team.
context: Senior advisory leader inside KPMG's national data practice. Three jobs at once: technical sales, delivery management and architecture — with teams of 10–15 and full commercial accountability.

outcomes.text: Cut business-user time-to-insight and reduced data error rates by 35% by delivering an enterprise Modern Data Platform on Snowflake plus Informatica IDMC (MDM, Data Quality, AXON catalog), giving clients trusted master data and genuine self-service analytics.

Reduced compliance remediation cost by architecting an enterprise data governance programme — policy engine, stewardship operating model, DQ KPIs and metadata taxonomy — that let clients pass regulatory audits.

Designed and delivered AI/ML Ops solutions for a large automobile manufacturer, building GenAI/RAG-ready data architecture with governed vector store integration and LLM-ready pipelines, adopted across three client production environments.
Developed an enterprise policy engine integrating organisational policy, technical metadata, data quality and data privacy requirements into enforceable controls.

Built a TOGAF-aligned enterprise data architecture practice — architecture views, roadmaps, review methods and implementation standards — using Spark, Erwin and PowerDesigner for architectural modelling.

leadership: Managed multi-engagement P&L including margin targets and revenue forecasts; led pricing strategy, effort estimation and proposal financial modelling; owned hiring, workforce planning, interviewing, onboarding and succession planning; ran performance management, mentoring and career development for architects, data engineers and solution leads across onshore and offshore delivery centres and time zones.

role: VP, Business Solutions Manager — AML & Analytics
headline: Anti-money-laundering transaction hub, where a false positive costs money and a false negative costs the licence.
context: Owned the data integration solution roadmap and architecture for the AML Transaction Hub, analytics, self-service reporting, search analytics and predictive analytics.

outcomes.text: Delivered an AML Transaction Hub integrating fifteen-plus data sources, enabling real-time suspicious activity detection, improving SAR filing accuracy by 30% and meeting OCC/FinCEN regulatory obligations on schedule.

Lowered false positive rates in transaction monitoring through automated data cleansing pipelines and an enterprise data governance framework for the AML domain — materially reducing analyst review cost.
Established data stewardship roles, policies and procedures; delivered conceptual and logical data models and ran vendor and tooling evaluation for AML and risk data solutions.
Led big data architecture and the delivery teams implementing risk, compliance and analytics projects.

leadership: Bridged compliance officers, model risk, technology and analytics teams — the role required translating regulatory obligation into architecture constraints engineers could actually build against.

headline: A metadata-driven data hub product — the idea that metadata should be executable, ten years early.
context: Architected a software product that let organisations leverage metadata from across their systems to rapidly assemble enterprise data hubs built on enterprise models in a NoSQL database.

outcomes.text: Designed a metadata-driven architecture where hub content could be consumed immediately across enterprise patterns — data integration, BI/analytics and microservices — without rebuilding per consumer.
Proved out enterprise-model-on-NoSQL patterns for accelerating metadata reuse and data hub assembly.
The core premise — that metadata should be runtime infrastructure rather than documentation — is the same argument I now make about the context layer for agentic AI.

leadership: Owned the product architecture and its technical narrative end to end, in a small-team environment where the architect also has to sell the idea.

role: Data Architect — Enterprise Canonical Data Model
headline: The canonical model behind a health insurer's business transformation — and an early bet on graph for MDM.
context: Created the vision and led implementation of the enterprise data modelling and integration hub capability at Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Carolina, supporting an enterprise-wide business transformation programme.

outcomes.text: Architected the Enterprise Canonical Data Model powering the transformation — consistent data exchange across twenty-plus integration touchpoints, and 40% faster integration builds through reusable canonical patterns.
Reduced duplicate master records by pioneering Neo4j graph database for MDM entity resolution — laying the foundation for a scalable enterprise MDM programme.
Built canonicals usable across REST services, ETL and messaging integration patterns, rather than a separate model per channel.
Ran proofs-of-concept on emerging platforms including Hadoop and graph databases well before either was a default enterprise choice.

leadership: Created and led a new enterprise data modelling and integration hub group from scratch — including making the case for its existence.

headline: Data strategy for liquidity risk in the middle of the post-2008 regulatory rebuild.
context: Defined the vision and roadmap for the data strategy and solutions supporting Liquidity Risk Management systems.

outcomes.text: Delivered a comprehensive architecture and governance roadmap for liquidity risk data, supporting post-2008 regulatory capital and liquidity reporting with auditable, fit-for-purpose data architecture.
Evaluated tools and technologies against regulatory reporting constraints rather than feature lists.

leadership: A short, sharp engagement — brought in to give a risk function a defensible data position under regulatory time pressure.

headline: Six years where architecture and delivery accountability sat on the same desk.
context: Consulting across Duke Energy (IBM), The Hanover Insurance Group, Teradyne and ADP — data architecture, solution architecture, delivery management and programme management.

outcomes.text: Delivered enterprise data warehousing, BI and analytics, metadata management, MDM, data cleansing, data quality and data governance solutions across financial services, insurance and energy.
Carried architecture depth and full delivery-management accountability simultaneously across multi-year engagements — the habit that later made advisory-director work straightforward.
Built the client-facing muscle: scoping, estimating, staffing, and then being answerable for the result.

leadership: Programme and delivery management across concurrent client accounts, including the uncomfortable part — owning the estimate you produced.

role: Associate Consultant → Regional Practice Manager, BI & Data Warehousing
headline: Where the people-leadership half of the career was built — running a practice, not just a project.
context: Started in delivery and moved into regional practice leadership for the Business Intelligence and Data Warehousing practice.

outcomes.text: Ran client relationship management, account management, pre-sales and sales, resource management, recruiting, training, pipeline planning and budgeting for the regional BI/DW practice.
Built packaged domain solution offerings for financial services, insurance, life sciences and government verticals — reusable IP rather than bespoke every time.
Owned mentoring and performance reviews for practice staff, at the point in a career where most architects are still avoiding people management.

leadership: This is where the leadership track started: hiring, developing and being accountable for a practice's people and its pipeline at the same time.
